questions.question: Find the surface area of a sphere whose diameter is equal to 28 cm.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of the sphere = 28 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Surface Area of a Sphere = 4 × π × r²

**Calculation:**

Radius of the sphere = Diameter / 2

Radius = 28 / 2 = 14 cm.

Surface Area = 4 × π × r²

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × π × 14²

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × π × 196

⇒ Surface Area = 784 × π

**The surface area of the sphere is 784π cm².**

questions.question:
A hollow spherical shell is made of a metal of density 3 g/cm3. Its internal and external radius are 15 cm and 18 cm, respectively. What is the weight (in kg) of the shell ?

{Take } pi = (22)/(7)
questions.solution:
Given:

Density of metal = 3 g/cm3

Internal radius (r1) = 15 cm

External radius (r2) = 18 cm

Value of π = 22/7

**Formulas used:**

Volume of hollow sphere = (4/3) × π × (r23 - r13)

Mass = Density × Volume

Weight (in kg) = Mass (in grams) / 1000

**Calculation:**

Calculate the Volume of the hollow sphere:

Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × (183 - 153)

Calculate the cubes:

183 = 18 × 18 × 18 = 5832 cm3

153 = 15 × 15 × 15 = 3375 cm3

Difference in volumes:

(r23 - r13) = 5832 - 3375 = 2457 cm3

Now, substitute this back into the volume formula:

Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × 2457

Volume = (88 / 21) × 2457

Volume = 10296 cm3

Calculate the Mass of the shell:

Mass = Density × Volume

Mass = 3 g/cm3 × 10296 cm3

Mass = 30888 g

Convert Mass to Weight in kilograms:

Since 1 kg = 1000 g,

Weight = 30888 g / 1000

Weight = 30.888 kg

The weight of the shell is: 30.888 kg

questions.question: A hollow spherical shell is made of a metal of density 36 g/cm³ . Its internal and external radius are 9 cm and 11 cm, respectively. What is the weight (in kg) of the shell ? (Take π = (22)/(7))

π = 22/7

Mass = Density × Volume

1 kg = 1000 g

⇒ V = (4/3) × (22/7) × (1331 - 729)

⇒ V = (4/3) × (22/7) × 602

⇒ V = (88/21) × 602

⇒ V = 88 × (602 / 21)

⇒ V = 88 × 28.666... cm³ (approximately)

⇒ V = 2522.666... cm³

⇒ Mass = Density × Volume

Convert mass to kilograms:

⇒ Weight = 90.816 kg

**∴ The weight of the shell is approximately 90.816 kg.**

questions.question: A solid sphere of diameter 6 cm is melted and then cast into cylindrical wire of radius 0.3 cm. Find the length of the wire.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of the solid sphere = 6 cm

Radius of the solid sphere (r) = 6 cm / 2 = 3 cm

Radius of the cylindrical wire (R) = 0.3 cm

**Formula used:**

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³

Volume of cylinder = πR²h

Volume of sphere = Volume of cylinder

**Calculation:**

Volume of sphere = (4/3)π(3)³

⇒ Volume of sphere = (4/3)π(27) = 36π cm³

Volume of cylinder = π(0.3)²h

⇒ 36π = π(0.09)h

⇒ h = 36 / 0.09 = 400 cm

⇒ h = 4 m

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: A cube of side 5 cm is cut into smaller cubes of side 1 cm. What is the ratio of the total surface area of the larger cube and the sum of the total surfaces of all the smaller cubes?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Side of the larger cube = 5 cm

Side of each smaller cube = 1 cm

**Formula Used:**

Surface Area of a Cube = 6 × (side)²

Ratio = Surface Area of Larger Cube / Sum of Surface Areas of Smaller Cubes

**Calculation:**

Surface area of the larger cube:

Surface Area = 6 × 5²

⇒ 6 × 25 = 150 cm²

Number of smaller cubes = (5/1)³ = 125 cubes

Surface area of one smaller cube = 6 × 1² = 6 cm²

Total surface area of all smaller cubes = 6 × 125 = 750 cm²

Ratio = 150 : 750

⇒ 1 : 5

**The ratio of the total surface area of the larger cube to the sum of the total surfaces of all the smaller cubes is 1:5.**

questions.question: A conical tent has to accommodate 30 persons. Each person must have 5 m² spaces on the ground and 120 m³ of air to breathe. Find the height (in m) of the tent.

Space per person = 5 m²

Air volume per person = 120 m³

**Formula used:**

Volume of cone V = (1/3)πr²h

Base area A = πr²

Total base area = n × space per person

Total volume = n × air volume per person

Formula used = 

volume of cone = (1/3) × area of base × height

Calculation:

Since each person will require 5 m2 of base area

So, the total base area required will be = 5 × 30 = 150 m2

 π × r2 = 150

Since each person will require 120 m3 of air 

So, Total Volume of air required will be = 30 × 120 = 3600 m3

Let the height of the cone be H m.

questions.question: The radius of the base of a right circular cone is 21 m and its curved surface area is 1914 m² . Find the volume (in m³ ) of the cone.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the base (r) = 21 m

Curved surface area (CSA) = 1914 m²

**Formula Used:**

Curved surface area of a cone (CSA) = πrl

Volume of a cone (V) = (1/3)πr²h

Using Pythagoras theorem, l² = r² + h²

**Calculation:**

Curved surface area of a cone (CSA) = πrl

1914 = π × 21 × l

⇒ l = 1914 / (π × 21)

⇒ l = 1914 / (22/7 × 21)

⇒ l = 1914 × 7 / (22 × 21)

⇒ l = 1914 / 66

⇒ l = 29 m

Using the Pythagoras theorem.

l² = r² + h²

29² = 21² + h²

841 = 441 + h²

⇒ h² = 841 - 441

⇒ h² = 400

⇒ h = 20 m

Volume of a cone (V) = (1/3)πr2h

V = (1/3)π × 21² × 20

V = (1/3) × (22/7) × 441 × 20

V = (1/3) × 22 × 63 × 20

V = 22 × 21 × 20

V = 9240 m³

**The volume of the cone is 9240 m³.**

questions.question: A cylindrical rod has an outer curved surface area of 4500 cm² . If the length of the rod is 39 cm, then the outer radius (in cm) of the rod, correct to two places of decimal, is: Take π = (22)/(7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The curved surface area (CSA) of a cylinder is given by 2 × π × r × h.

Radius (r) = CSA ÷ (2 × π × h)

r = 4500 ÷ (2 × 22/7 × 39)

r = (4500 × 7) ÷ 1716 = 31500 ÷ 1716

r = 18.356... ≈ 18.36 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18.36 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00f207f957454c35a33fc84504f64a839019f6bea2a4c5d1faa0e3961c8ba25e.png] 

**Given:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of the cylinder = 4500 cm²

Length (height, h) of the rod = 39 cm

Let the outer radius of the rod be r.

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area of a cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (22 ÷ 7) × r × 39 = 4500

⇒ (1716 ÷ 7) × r = 4500

⇒ r = (4500 × 7) ÷ 1716

⇒ r = 31500 ÷ 1716

⇒ r = 2625 ÷ 143

⇒ r = 18.3566... cm

⇒ Rounding to two decimal places, r ≈ 18.36 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18.36 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cylinder

The TSA includes the curved surface and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cylinder

The amount of space contained within the cylinder is calculated using the base area times height: V = πr²h.

Hollow Cylinder

If the rod was a hollow tube with an outer radius R and an inner radius r, the volume of material used would be V = πh(R² − r²).

questions.question: If the radius of a hemisphere is increased by 50%, then find the percentage increase in surface area.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial radius = r

New radius = r + 50% of r = 1.5r

**Formula used:**

Surface area of hemisphere = 3πr²

**Calculation:**

Old surface area = 3πr²

New surface area = 3π(1.5r)² = 3π × 2.25r² = 6.75πr²

Percentage increase = [(New - Old) / Old] × 100

= [(6.75πr² - 3πr²) / 3πr²] × 100

= (3.75πr² / 3πr²) × 100

= (1.25) × 100 = 125%

**∴ Surface area increases by 125%**

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 60 cm, 75 cm, and 45 cm. What is its area? (in cm² )
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sides of the triangle: a = 60 cm, b = 75 cm, c = 45 cm

**Formula used:**

Area of a triangle (using Heron’s formula):

Area = sqrt{s × (s - a) × (s - b) × (s - c)}

Where s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2 (semi-perimeter)

**Calculation:**

s = (60 + 75 + 45) ÷ 2

⇒ s = 180 ÷ 2 = 90 cm

Area = sqrt{90 × (90 - 60) × (90 - 75) × (90 - 45)}

⇒ Area = sqrt{90 × 30 × 15 × 45}

⇒ Area = sqrt{1822500}

⇒ Area = 1350 cm²

**∴ The area of the triangle is 1350 cm².**

questions.question: The diameter of the base of a solid cone is 24 cm and its height is 21 cm. It is cut into three parts by two cuts which are parallel to its base. The cuts are at the height of 7 cm and 14 cm from the base, respectively. Find the curved surface area (in cm² ) of the top part. (use π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Height of the top cone = 21 − 14 = 7 cm.

By similarity, top radius r = (7 ÷ 21) × 12 = 4 cm.

Slant height l = √(4² + 7²) = √65 cm.

Curved Surface Area = 3.14 × 4 × √65 = 12.56√65 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 12.56√65 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Height of cone (H) = 21 cm, Base diameter = 24 cm ⇒ Radius (R) = 12 cm. Cuts at 7 cm and 14 cm from the base.

Formula Used: CSA of cone = πrl, Slant height l = √(r² + h²), Similarity ratio r/R = h/H.

 

 
 

 
 

 
 
•

 Base Radius (R) = 12 cm
 Total H = 21 cm

⇒ The top part is the portion from height 14 cm to 21 cm (from base).

⇒ Height of top cone (h) = 21 − 14 = 7 cm.

⇒ By similarity of triangles: r ÷ 12 = 7 ÷ 21 ⇒ r = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 cm.

⇒ Slant height of top part (l) = √(4² + 7²) = √(16 + 49) = √65 cm.

⇒ Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 3.14 × 4 × √65 = 12.56√65 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 12.56√65 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of Similar Cones

When a cone is cut by a plane parallel to the base, the ratio of the radii and heights are equal: r₁/r₂ = h₁/h₂.

Volume Ratio

The ratio of the volumes of two similar cones is equal to the cube of the ratio of their corresponding heights: V₁/V₂ = (h₁/h₂)³.

CSA of a Frustum

The curved surface area of the middle or bottom parts (frustums) is calculated as π × (R + r) × l, where l is the slant height of that segment.</p

questions.question: A water tank is in the form of a right circular cone with radius 3 m and height 14 m. The tank is filled with water at the rate of one cubic metre per second. Find the time taken, in minutes, to fill the tank.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the water tank (r) = 3 m

Height of the water tank (h) = 14 m

Rate of water filling = 1 cubic metre per second

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cone = (1/3)πr²h

Time taken to fill the tank = Volume / Rate of filling

**Calculation:**

Volume of the tank = (1/3)πr²h

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × π × (3)² × 14

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × π × 9 × 14

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × π × 126

⇒ Volume = 42π

Volume ≈ 42 × 3.14

Volume ≈ 131.88 cubic metres

Time taken = Volume / Rate of filling

⇒ Time taken = 131.88 / 1

⇒ Time taken = 131.88 seconds

Convert seconds to minutes:

⇒ Time taken = 131.88 / 60

⇒ Time taken ≈ 2.2 minutes

**The time taken to fill the tank is 2.2 minutes.**

questions.question: Two right circular cones have heights in the ratio 1 : 9 and their base perimeters are in the ratio 9: 5. Determine their volume (Use π = (22/7))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Height ratio of two cones = 1 : 9

Base perimeter ratio of two cones = 9 : 5

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cone = (1)/(3) pi r² h

**Calculation:**

Let the height of the first cone be h₁ and the second cone be h₂.

h₁ / h₂ = 1 / 9

Let the base radius of the first cone be r₁ and the second cone be r₂.

Base perimeter P = 2πr

So, P₁ / P₂ = 2πr₁ / 2πr₂

r₁ / r₂ = 9 / 5

Let the volume of the first cone be V₁ and the second cone be V₂.

Volume of the first cone:

V₁ = (1)/(3) pi r₁² h₁

Volume of the second cone:

V₂ = (1)/(3) pi r₂² h₂

We need to find the ratio V₁ / V₂:

V₁ / V₂ = (frac{1)/(3) pi r₁² h₁}{(1)/(3) pi r₂² h₂}

V₁ / V₂ = (r₁² h₁)/(r₂² h₂)

V₁ / V₂ = ((9 / 5)² × (1 / 9))/(1)

V₁ / V₂ = (81 / 25 × 1 / 9)/(1)

V₁ / V₂ = (81 / 225)/(1)

V₁ / V₂ = 9 / 25

**The ratio of their volumes is 9 : 25.**

questions.question: The volume of a conical tent is 9240 m³ and the area of its base is 1386 m². What is the length of the canvas required to build the tent if the width of canvas is 3 m? (Use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The volume of a conical tent (V) = 9240 m³

The area of its base (A) = 1386 m²

Width of the canvas = 3 m

**Formula used:**

Volume of a cone: V = dfrac{1}{3}pi r² h

Area of the base: A = pi r²

Slant height (l) = sqrt{r² + h²}

Length of canvas = dfrac{{Curved surface area}}{{Width of canvas}}

Curved surface area = pi r l

**Calculation:**

pi r² = 1386

⇒ dfrac{22}{7} r² = 1386

⇒ r² = dfrac{1386 times 7}{22}

⇒ r² = 441

⇒ r = 21 m

Volume (V) = dfrac{1}{3} pi r² h

9240 = dfrac{1}{3} times dfrac{22}{7} times 21² times h

⇒ 9240 = dfrac{1}{3} times 22 times 21 times 21 times h

⇒ 9240 = 462 h

⇒ h = dfrac{9240}{462}

⇒ h = 20 m

Slant height (l) = sqrt{r² + h²}

⇒ l = sqrt{21² + 20²}

⇒ l = sqrt{841}

⇒ l = 29 m

Curved surface area = pi r l

⇒ Curved surface area = dfrac{22}{7} times 21 times 29

⇒ Curved surface area = 22 times 3 times 29

⇒ Curved surface area = 1914 m²

Length of canvas = dfrac{1914}{3}

⇒ Length of canvas = 638 m

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: A conical tent has to accommodate 40 persons. Each person requires 5 m² space on the ground and 70 m³ of air to breathe. Find the height (in m) of the tent (use π = 22/7).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A conical tent has to accommodate 40 persons. Each person requires 5 m² of ground space and 70 m³ of air to breathe.

**Formula used:**

Volume of cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h

**Solution:**

Each person requires 5 m² of base area.

⇒ Total base area required = 5 × 40 = 200 m²

π × r² = 200

Since each person will require 70 m3 of air 

⇒ Total volume of air required = 40 × 70 = 2800 m³

Let the height of the cone be h m.

(1/3) × π × r² × h = 2800

⇒ (1/3) × 200 × h = 2800

⇒ h = 2800 ÷ 200 × 3

⇒ h = 42

**∴ The height of the conical tent is 42 m.**

questions.question: A cylinder of height 13 cm is made from a rectangular sheet of dimension 44 cm x 13 cm, without any cut. What is the total surface closed from both ends? (Use π = (22)/(7))

The length of the rectangular sheet forms the circumference of the base of the cylinder.

So, C = 44 cm

⇒ 2π r = 44

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 44

⇒ r = (44 × 7)/(2 × 22) = 7 cm

Now, we calculate the total surface area of the cylinder.

TSA = 2π r h + 2(π r²)

⇒ TSA = 2 × (22)/(7) × 7 × 13 + 2 × (22)/(7) × 7 × 7

⇒ TSA = 2 × 22 × 13 + 2 × 22 × 7

⇒ TSA = 572 + 308

⇒ TSA = 880 cm²

**The total surface closed from both ends is 880 cm².**
